newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's national parks threatened by loggers.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's national parks threatened by loggers.

text.p: Cambodia's national parks and wildlife preserves have become easy targets for illegal loggers, endangering the country's few remaining environmental resources, government environmental officials said on Wednesday.
"The parks are already jeopardised, it's unbelievable," said a senior Environment Ministry official who asked not to be identified.
He said he had seen heavily armed soldiers in recent days blocking roads into at least two national parks to facilitate alleged illegal logging.

The government banned all log exports on December 31, 1996, and has vowed to stop all new timber cutting but concedes it does not have control over all forests, especially in areas controlled by former Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
Secret logging continued unhindered in protected areas, environmental officials said, adding that they were powerless to deal with the situation.
"I told my boss, but what can we do?" said one.
Secretary of State for Defence Ek Sereywath said the role being played by soldiers was a problem, particularly in parks near the border of Thailand and Vietnam.
"But the problem is that we have issued orders and directives to make them respect the government, but in some cases their salary is so low, they are so tempted," he said.
The average soldier's salary was $35 a month, he said.
Minister of Environment Mok Mareth told Reuters that Kirrirom National Park in southern Cambodia was in particular danger.
A British lobby group, Global Witness, said on Wednesday that trucks loaded with hard wood from the park were being moved out earlier this week under escort from soldiers, who also blocked off roads.
Cambodia has seven national parks, 11 wildlife sanctuaries, and five other protected areas.
